concept.name: Minting
concept.definition: Minting is the creation of new tokens on-chain, increasing total supply — whether as protocol issuance (block rewards to miners/validators) or as application-level token creation by smart contracts.
concept.intuition: It is the printing press of a token economy: new units come into existence by rule, either paying for security or instantiating new assets.
concept.mechanics: At the protocol layer, minting follows the consensus issuance schedule: Bitcoin's coinbase transaction creates new BTC for the block's miner, and Ethereum issues new ETH to validators for proposals and attestations. At the application layer, contracts mint tokens (e.g. LP tokens on deposit, LSTs on staking, NFTs on purchase) according to their code; unbacked or infinite-mint bugs are a classic exploit.
concept.failure_modes: Smart contract minting flaws (infinite mint, unbacked mint) let attackers fabricate supply and drain pools or depeg assets; at the protocol level, minting is inflation that dilutes holders unless offset by demand or burns.
concept.misconceptions: Mining and minting are related but distinct: PoW miners and PoS validators earn newly minted issuance, but 'minting' also covers any contract-created token. Newly minted rewards are not free value — their cost is dilution of all holders.
concept.example: Depositing 5 ETH into Lido mints ~5 stETH to your wallet (application-level mint), while Ethereum's protocol simultaneously mints small new ETH amounts every slot to pay validators (protocol issuance).
